name: Kang-Petrov Arms KPA-16A 'Adjustable'
description:
The KPA-16A is the suppressor-optimized variant of the KPA-16 platform, built around an adjustable low-profile gas block with five indexed positions and a recessed muzzle threading that accepts standard 5.56mm suppressor and muzzle device attachments without requiring a proprietary adapter. The barrel is 16 inches, medium-profile, with a 1:8 twist rate that stabilizes both standard 55-grain and heavier 77-grain subsonic loads. The bolt carrier group runs a nickel boron coating for reduced friction and easier cleaning under the increased carbon load of suppressed fire. The lower receiver incorporates an enhanced buffer and heavier recoil spring to manage the increased backpressure of suppressed cycling without carrier-tilt issues that plagued earlier KP suppressed configurations. The handguard is free-floating over the barrel for accuracy benefits and features a full-length M-LOK layout that accommodates the additional hardware — light, laser aiming device, suppressor clearance — that suppressed operators typically run.

Kang-Petrov developed the KPA-16A in response to the growing GLMZ market for suppressed civilian firearms — a market segment that has expanded significantly since Meridian PD's dissolution left acoustic signature management as a civilian concern rather than a law-enforcement-only capability. The rifle is priced at the upper Tier 1 range and requires a standard suppressor license for the muzzle threading to be activated — it ships with a thread protector installed and the threading documentation sealed, which Kang-Petrov's legal team considers sufficient compliance with GLMZ registration requirements. Street opinion on whether this actually constitutes compliance varies.

The KPA-16A's five-position gas block is the feature operators discuss most, and debate is ongoing about the optimal setting for various suppressor lengths and ammunition types. GLMZ street armorers have produced an unofficial reference card — printed on waterproof material and sized to fit inside the rifle's stock storage compartment — that maps gas block positions to common suppressor models and ammunition types. The fact that an unofficial reference card exists and circulates widely tells you something about both the rifle's popularity and the inadequacy of Kang-Petrov's official documentation.
specifications: caliber: 5.56mm Combat Standard effective_range: 400m (300m subsonic) rate_of_fire: Semi-automatic magazine_capacity: 30 rounds weight: 3.2 kg
tactical_use: The KPA-16A is built for operators who run suppressors regularly — not as an accessory but as a standard operating condition. The adjustable gas block allows tuning for specific suppressor volumes and ammunition weights, which matters for both reliability and sound reduction optimization. Operators running subsonic 77-grain loads for maximum sound reduction must reduce the gas setting to prevent bolt-over-travel; the five-position block provides enough adjustment range to accommodate most commercial suppressor sizes. Standard tactical configuration is rifle plus suppressor plus low-power variable optic plus weapon light on a sling.
cultural_context: In post-Meridian GLMZ, acoustic management is no longer just a military concern. The KPA-16A represents the civilianization of suppressed-fire doctrine — it's bought by people who have decided that sound discipline matters in their operating environment. That encompasses a wide range of actors, from genuinely safety-conscious outer-ring operators who don't want to damage their hearing in enclosed defense scenarios, to fixers who have professional reasons to avoid acoustic signatures, to people whose reasons don't bear close examination. The licensing requirement creates a paper trail that some buyers consider a feature and others consider a liability.
known_users: outer-ring home defense with suppressor license
story_hooks: A KPA-16A suppressor license was issued to a shelf worker in a Slagworks manufacturing zone six months ago — unremarkable on its face, except that the same license number appears on three other KPA-16A registrations in different GLMZ boroughs under different names, which means either a registration system compromise or someone inside the licensing office is selling duplicate documentation.

An armorer known for producing the unofficial gas block reference cards has gone quiet — their usual distribution channels have dried up, and the last person who tried to contact them found their workshop cleared out but not abandoned: the equipment is gone, the personal effects are still there, and someone left a KPA-16A with the gas block set to position zero, which means suppressed, subsonic, and nearly silent.
